$comment: The contributor community (/contributing/; /roles/, /pin/ and /contributors/ redirect here). Unlisted (noindex, not linked from the program page) until the board approves the ranks. Sells joining the contributor community and working your way up: anyone can contribute; roles; the Contributing Member pin; Reviewer, Committer and Maintainer each add a ring and a responsibility. The pins are live 3D on desktop. Summarises design/research/recognition-system.md. [PLACEHOLDER] marks what's still open.
title: Contributing
description: Join the people who build The Upskilling Labs. Anyone can contribute; the ones who keep at it earn the pin, then the rings, and the trust that comes with each.
draft: A working draft. The board hasn't approved the ranks yet, and the pins are still being made.

title: Build
The Labs
hero.lede: Anyone can contribute. Keep at it, and you earn the pin, then the rings, and more of the work to lead.
hero.status: First pins: our two steering committees
hero.pinAlt: The Contributing Member pin, turning to follow your pointer

start.title: Some people use the playbook. Some people write the next page.
start.lede: The Labs is built by the people in it. Pick a way in.

items.label: Contribute
items.title: Make something better.
items.body: A playbook, a flyer, a kit, a line of code. Anyone can suggest a change, and you're credited by name.

items.label: Take a role
items.title: Do it in public.
items.body: Upskiller, Poderator, Mentor, Ambassador. Get trained, then practise until the role's lead says you've got it. Ambassador is open now.

items.label: Get recognized
items.title: Earn the pin.
items.body: When The Labs runs on something you made, the people who saw it put your name forward.

rings.title: Every ring is earned.
rings.lede: The pin says you contributed. Each ring says you're trusted with more. Scroll, and watch it grow.

steps.line: You made something we now run on.
steps.how: Recognized for real work on The Labs itself, with a line on the register saying what it was.

steps.line: You've done it, so you can judge it.
steps.how: A Practitioner in two roles, sponsored by two pin holders from different roles or Labs.
steps.trusted: Reviewing changes, and new Practitioners, in the roles you know.

steps.line: You've helped everywhere. Now you can say yes.
steps.how: You've helped in every core area of The Labs.
steps.trusted: Approving changes to your Lab's playbooks, within a written grant from the board.

steps.line: You set the standard others build to.
steps.how: Nominated by Maintainers, confirmed by the board.
steps.trusted: Setting the direction for an area. The board keeps the final say.

rings.names: Rank names are drafts, borrowed from open-source projects, until the board decides. [PLACEHOLDER]

metal.title: The metal says where you did the work.
metal.lede: Brass for your region. Silver for work across the whole network. Same pin, same rings.
metal.stageLabel: The {rank} pin in {metal}. Drag, or use the arrow keys, to turn it.

given.title: It starts with the work. It ends with a handshake.

steps.title: Do the work.
steps.body: Make something The Labs can reuse, or practise the roles a rank asks for.

steps.title: Someone vouches.
steps.body: Pin holders put your name forward. For a ring, that's two sponsors, from different roles or Labs.

steps.title: It's recorded.
steps.body: Your Lab checks it, and HQ writes it on the register with a line on what you did.

steps.title: Pinned.
steps.body: At the next regional gathering. Your sponsors pin it on and say a sentence about why.

decides.title: Ranks recognize. Boards decide.
rules: The pin is yours for good. Permissions come with an active seat, granted by the board in writing.
Ranks carry no vote. The boards run programs, money, people and the brand.
No one can buy a pin, a ring, or a vote.
It's recognition, not certification. It's the community saying thank you.
Step back whenever you need to. You keep the pin and the title.

join.title: Every pin starts with one contribution.
join.lede: The way in today is the ambassador program. Tell your story, bring someone to their first workshop, and see what you end up building.

footer.renders: Images of the pin are 3D renders, not photos. The real pins are still being made.
